title: How to Install Thermostatic Radiator Valves | This Old House
summary: This video provides a practical walkthrough for installing a thermostatic radiator valve (TRV) on an older radiator. It covers removing an existing valve assembly (including the valve body, nipple, and spud) with a spud wrench, preparing the new valve with thread sealant and wick, and using pipe dope on old piping. The demonstration then shows aligning and connecting the valve, routing a sensor through the radiator cover, securing the sensor with zip screws, installing a cover plate, and completing the final connections. The steps emphasize making a tight seal at the spud and careful handling of the sensor path within the radiator assembly.
topics: drilling a small hole for sensor

sections.title: Dismantling old valve hardware
sections.description: Loosen and remove the valve body from the threaded nipple, then extract the spud with a spud wrench.

sections.title: Preparing and installing the new valve
sections.description: Apply thread sealant to the first few threads, replace the spud with a new one, use single strand wicking to fill thread voids, and apply pipe dope while preparing the old pipe. Then square the valve and begin making the connections.

sections.title: Routing and securing the sensor
concepts: drilling a small hole for sensor
sections.description: Drill a small hole as needed to route the sensor element, feed the sensor through the opening, and secure it to the side of the radiator cover with zip screws.

sections.title: Final connections and finish
sections.description: Install the cover plate to conceal the securing screws and complete the final valve connections, ensuring everything seats properly.
